institution: National Centre for Disease Control, National AMR Surveillance Network (NARS-Net)
citation: National Centre for Disease Control. Annual Report: National Antimicrobial Resistance Surveillance Network (NARS-Net), reporting period 1 January 2021 to 31 December 2021. New Delhi: National Programme on AMR Containment, NCDC, Directorate General of Health Services, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare; 2022.
reporting: Number tested, number resistant and percent resistant (%R, whole numbers), by pathogen and specimen type (blood, pus aspirate, other sterile body fluids, urine), all location types combined; blood also charted by location type (emergency, inpatient, outpatient, ICU) with printed data labels but no isolate numbers per location.
method: WHONET; CLSI guidelines (edition not stated); one result per patient, specimen type and pathogen, the first isolate of a species in the period (96,370 isolates reported, 87,996 unique patient isolates analysed); disk diffusion, broth microdilution or automated AST; colistin by broth microdilution (CLSI M02 and M100) for a limited number of isolates; vancomycin-resistant S. aureus and colistin-resistant Gram-negatives counted only after confirmation at the AMR-NRL, NCDC.

verification.note: Tables 4 to 10 parsed from the PDF text layer (PyMuPDF words; each value assigned to its specimen column and to the number tested, number resistant or %R sub-column by x position; multi-line drug names joined) and every value then compared by eye with the pages rendered at scale 2.2 (the denser tables also cropped into halves). Every printed %R was recomputed from the printed number resistant and number tested: all agree within rounding except the 13 Table 6 cells recorded as conflicts. Table 2 counts transcribed from the text layer, compared with the page and checked against its column totals and the report total (87,996 with the one stool isolate named in the text on page 34). Location-type charts (Figures 9, 10, 12, 14, 15: vector horizontal clustered bars, labels in the text layer): each label assigned to the nearest category label in y and to its bar by its y offset from the category centre (bars run emergency, inpatient, outpatient, ICU from the top, the legend order, confirmed by sampling every chart's bar colours against the legend); every label was then checked against its bar by measuring the bar length on the rendered page (all within 0.6 percentage points). Each all-locations table value lies within the range of its location labels (emergency included). Page numbers are PDF page numbers (1-based).

notes: Fifth NARS-Net annual report: 35 medical college laboratories in 25 states and UTs, seven priority bacterial pathogens, January to December 2021 (first isolate per patient, specimen type and pathogen). All figures are percent resistant as printed, in whole numbers (intermediate counted as not resistant). Specimens: pus aspirate (PA) is shown under deep infections (aspirates); other sterile body fluids (OSBF) as sterile body fluids. Table rows combine all location types (set all). Location rows (ward, outpatient, ICU) come from blood bar charts with printed data labels; this report charts emergency department isolates as a separate series (not recorded) and prints no isolate numbers per location, so those rows have no n. The E. coli table (Table 6) contradicts itself for blood (11 drugs) and for urine piperacillin/tazobactam and TMP/SMX: see the row conflicts. Colistin percentages are blank for Klebsiella, Pseudomonas, Acinetobacter and E. coli urine (counts only, see excluded). The S. aureus location chart (Figure 8) reproduces the Enterococcus chart, so there are no S. aureus location rows. Only S. Typhi has percentages for Salmonella. No fungal data in this edition.
issues: Second reader 2026-09-26: the seeded sample of 94 of 378 cells (36 of them chart labels) was read from the page images, then every other cell as well: all 378 cells, the number tested and number resistant of all 243 table cells, all 39 row n and all 25 counts (Table 2 and the stool isolate named on page 34), pages rendered at scale 2.5 and tables cropped at scale 4. 0 transcription errors, nothing corrected. The validator's caution list prints the values of the 17 caution cells, so those (3 of them in the sample) were not read blind; they were confirmed on the page and in the PDF text layer.

Chart rows (Figures 9, 10, 12, 14, 15; horizontal bars run emergency, inpatient, outpatient, ICU from the top): every label checked against its bar with the PDF vector geometry (bar colour against the legend swatch, bar length within 0.5 points of the label). Also confirmed: the Figure 15 bars without labels (imipenem emergency and outpatient, meropenem outpatient and ICU); Figure 8 (S. aureus title) repeats Figure 9 label for label; the Figure 9 amikacin (10, 27, 24, 36) and amoxicillin/clavulanic acid (78, 57, 43, 61) labels repeat Figure 10.

All 17 caution cells are printed as recorded and their conflict texts are accurate. Enterococcus blood linezolid: Table 5 prints 3% (40 of 1,582) and Figure 9 prints 1, 2, 3 and 3% (emergency, inpatient, outpatient, ICU), while the executive summary (PDF page 10) says 8.4% and page 26 says linezolid-resistant VRE rose to 8.4%.

E. coli blood, Table 6: the printed number resistant gives the printed % only for amoxicillin/clavulanic acid and colistin; the 11 conflict counts are as printed. The printed % is the better supported figure: the text on PDF page 28 gives ampicillin over 80%, cefotaxime over 70%, carbapenem resistance up to 33%, ciprofloxacin 63%, TMP/SMX 54% and piperacillin/tazobactam 43%; every printed % lies within its Figure 10 labels (emergency included), while the count-derived values for amikacin (72), ampicillin (45), cefepime (82), cefotaxime (58), ciprofloxacin (8.7), ertapenem (52) and TMP/SMX (1.1) do not and meropenem's (981 of 854) is impossible; 10 of the 11 counts give another drug's printed % with that drug's number tested. Only gentamicin (39 printed, 34 from counts) and imipenem (29 printed, 31 from counts) are separated by neither the text nor the chart.

E. coli urine piperacillin/tazobactam 29% (2,937 of 2,937) and TMP/SMX 59% (8,918 of 8,918): number resistant printed equal to number tested; the page 28 text gives 59% for urine TMP/SMX. Pseudomonas blood ceftazidime location rows: Figure 14 prints 47 (inpatient), 34 (outpatient), 33 (ICU) and 27 (emergency); the text on PDF page 36 gives 46, 36, 35 and 28.

No count-table mismatch: the Table 2 Salmonella blood count of 150 is 148 S. Typhi (the row) plus 2 S. Paratyphi (counts only, excluded); the Table 2 column totals (19,097, 30,366, 4,023, 34,509) add up and, with the one stool isolate, give the report's 87,996.

Lead 2026-09-26: "Pus aspirate (PA)" (NCDC SOP category, aspirated pus, swabs excluded) filed under specimen "deep" (deep infections, aspirates), as for the other NCDC-protocol networks; 6 rows and 6 counts moved from "pus". E. coli blood: the conflicts on the six drugs whose printed percentage the page 28 text confirms are removed (second reader's evidence); the rest stay.
